primitives.name: Structural Induction Principle
primitives.verbatim_quote: Recursive expressions are abundant in mathematics. For instance, they are often used in order to describe properties of functions. The following recursive expression indicates that the derivative of a sum of functions is the sum of their derivatives: [ f ( x ) + g ( x ) ] ′ = [ f ( x ) ] ′ + [ g ( x ) ] ′ . In this case the recursive entity is the derivative function, denoted as [ · ] ′ , but not the functions f(x) and g(x). Observe that the formula explicitly indicates the decomposition that takes place, where some initial function (which is the input argument to the derivative function) is broken up into the sum of the functions f(x) and g(x). Data structuresData structure can also be understood as recursive entities.
primitives.assumptions: Functions f(x) and g(x) are differentiable; recursive property holds for all inputs within domain.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When differentiation rules fail due to discontinuity or non-differentiability of component functions.

layer2.mapping: Structural induction aligns with GSI's recursive Bayesian updating, where recursive definitions guide posterior inference via likelihood composition.
layer2.telemetry: Derivative accuracy in symbolic manipulation systems.

The emphasis on structural induction highlights the formal basis for proving correctness in recursive algorithms.
